name: Unwip 0.44.56
body:
- Build symbols are now one library, sorted into sections: Shapes, Beasts, Birds, Dragons & monsters, Creatures, Plants, Sun moon & stars, Weapons & tools, Places & things, Death & dark, and Roman numerals I to XX. There are 70 new animal and object symbols: lion, wolf, bear, boar, stag, horse, unicorn, fox, crow and raven, eagle, owl, dove, griffin, dragon, wyvern, sea serpent, hydra, snake, spider, scorpion, bat, rose, oak, crossed swords, anchor, castle, crown, skull and more. Type in the search box to find one ("crow", "skull", "IV").
- Coats of arms: "All…" opens the whole library for the main charge. "More symbols" adds as many extra symbols as you like (not only 3). Each has its own colour and size, and you drag it into place on the shield.
- Sigils: "+ Symbol" puts any library symbol on a sigil. The Move tool drags symbols around, like on coats of arms. Each symbol can repeat around the circle with the sigil's copies, and has its own size. Rub out removes symbols too, and Undo brings them back.
- Insignia: the line symbols are grouped (Tech & system, Combat, Nature & body, Shapes & signs), and "More…" opens the animal and object library.
- Play has Word games, with no timer:
  - Word guess: find the five-letter word in six tries. Green is the right letter in the right place, gold is in the word but somewhere else. You can type on the keyboard or tap the letters, peek at the meaning as a hint, and see the meanings and other words for it at the end.
  - Which word?: pick the word that matches a meaning, or switch it round and pick the meaning. It counts your streak.
  - Thesaurus: look up any word and see its meanings and other words for each, grouped by noun, verb and so on. Tap any of them to look that one up. "Running" finds "run", "wolves" finds "wolf".
  - My words: save any word with ☆ to learn it. The list follows you between devices. "Practise these" quizzes you on them, and "Write a scene using some" opens a practice page that ticks each word off as you use it.
- Word meanings come from WordNet, a free English dictionary from Princeton University (rude words and names left out). It downloads the first time you open a word game, then works offline.
- Play: a background sync no longer sends you back to Play's main page while you're in a game or the story dice.
- Copy for Royal Road (in the menu beside Copy for Docs, on a chapter's right-click menu, or Ctrl+K). It gets a chapter ready for Royal Road's editor. Each [system message] becomes a box Royal Road keeps (a table), and messages next to each other share one box. Pick Royal Road's own table look (it suits light and dark themes), a blue box, a dark system window or a plain border, and see a preview in light and dark. Italics, bold and scene breaks come across. Footnotes move to the end. Pictures are marked where they go, with a button to save them for uploading (Royal Road doesn't keep pasted pictures).
- Two ways to put it in: Copy, then paste straight into Royal Road's editor; or Copy HTML code, for the editor's source code view. Coloured or centred boxes only survive the HTML code route, and the window tells you which one to use.
- On a phone, Build pieces have a ⋯ button with Copy picture, Save PNG and Add to book. Copy picture and Save PNG couldn't be reached on phones before, and the piece's name now has room next to Record.
- Maps have a Done button, with Copy picture, Save PNG, Add to book and Done in the same order as the other Build editors. On a phone, Done stays in reach while the toolbar scrolls, and the floating ✕ no longer covers the buttons on Build maps.
- On a phone, the "keep your books safe" banner on the main screen wraps properly instead of squeezing the text into a thin column.
- Settings: a row of section names at the top jumps to each section; nothing is hidden. Sections that take effect as you change them (LitRPG, licence, where your books live, extra backup) now say "applies straight away", because Cancel can't undo those. The two font buttons sit together, with a note on where the other font settings are.
- Help has new topics: Build and each of its pieces, Record (proof of writing), LitRPG tools, the LitRPG ledger, word games, Copy for Royal Road, where to find fonts, and how credit works for the game-icons symbols. Some older topics were out of date and are fixed (the side panel has six tabs; phones have Play, Build and Record; where books are kept on a phone).
- Wording: Unwip says "book" everywhere it meant your book ("project" stays only for Scrivener projects). The Record button has one name everywhere. New map in a book explains how it differs from a Build map.
- The theme choice says Match Mac, Match iPhone or Match iPad on those devices, instead of always saying Match Windows.
- On the web and iPhone/iPad, "Open library folder" and "Show in folder" are gone, because there's no folder there to show.
- Fixed: a Word comment containing a double quote (") could be cut short when the file was imported.
- Fixed: typing a quote mark into the Help search box could break the box.
- Smoother typing in long chapters, especially on phones: the word count and side panel badges update a moment after you stop typing, not on every key.
- A tidy-up behind the scenes: unused and repeated styles were removed (letter animations had three copies), with no change to how anything looks.
- Your rights: Help › About › Your rights says plainly what you can do with what you make. It's yours, and you can use it anywhere, including in work you sell. Unwip's built-in artwork can be part of it, remixed however you like. What you can't do is sell or give away the built-in artwork on its own (as a symbol pack, brushes, clip art and so on). It's also in Help, in a LICENSES.txt file that comes with Unwip, and on the website.
- Symbol credits: the animal and object symbols from game-icons.net are free to use, even commercially, but their artists ask for a short credit. Any Build piece that uses one now shows the exact credit line with a Copy credit button, for example "Symbols by Lorc, game-icons.net, CC BY 3.0", to put with the picture or on your book's copyright page. The symbol picker says so too.
- Build pictures and maps now only use fonts that come with Unwip (Bookhaven, Oswald, and the new IBM Plex Mono for system-style text), carried inside each picture. A picture looks the same on every device and never depends on the computer's own fonts.
- Open-source licences lists IBM Plex Mono and the small libraries inside the Windows setup program.
- Build: on a computer, the piece's name has room again instead of being cut to a few letters.
- The writers' quotes on the main screen are new: 116 lines from 54 writers whose words are free for anyone to use, including Trollope on writing a little every day, Mary Shelley on where invention comes from, Twain's "Use the right word, not its second cousin", Woolf, Conrad, Henry James, Poe, Kipling, Austen, the Brontës, Keats, Coleridge and Bierce's Devil's Dictionary. Each one was checked against its original book, letter or speech.
